subject: Greenline: Custom premium response SKU and pilot crediting
messages:
From: Amit Sharma <amit@greenline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <procurement@greenline.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial questions on premium response SKU and pilot credits

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team liked the ability to pin model versions and the auto-fallback behavior. A few procurement and engineering questions came up while we were internalizing the offer: 

- Can you summarize the SLA tiers you recommend for a customer our size (100M tokens/month) and the incremental uplift in unit price for 99.95 vs 99.99 uptime?
- We run a 3-month pilot before committing to reserved capacity. Is there an upfront trial credit you can provide for the premium response pack? How are credits applied to retainer vs overages?
- We need clarity on escalation coverage windows and on-call response times (business hours vs 24x7). Can Redwood map those to the SKU line items?

If you can send a short one-pager with the SKU mapping and a sample invoice that shows how a pilot credit appears, that would speed internal review.

Appreciate it,
Amit
Senior Platform Engineer
Greenline Systems
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Sharma <amit@greenline.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <procurement@greenline.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on premium response SKU and pilot credits

Amit —

Great questions. I pulled the pricing and packaging team into this reply (Ben is cc'd) and attached a short quote + MAP workbook. High level answers below; see the attached PDF for precise per-token/unit math.

1) Recommended uptime tiers (typical for 100M tokens/month):
   - Standard (99.9): included with hosted API; baseline unit price.
   - Premium (99.95): ~+12% per-token uplift; includes 24x5 escalation and 60-minute P1 response SLAs during business hours.
   - Elite (99.99): ~+28% per-token uplift; includes 24x7 escalation, 15-minute P1 response SLA, dedicated on-call rotation, and quarterly runbooks.

2) Pilot crediting:
   - We can offer a one-time pilot credit up to $40k that applies first to usage over the pilot period. Credits are consumed against invoice line items in the following order: usage overages, then retainer fees, then ancillary services. For contract clarity we can tie the credit to a 3-month MAP with minimum engagement terms in the quote.

3) Escalation coverage mapping to SKUs:
   - Premium response SKU (PR-S1): business-hours P1 (60m), business-hours P2 (4h), 24x5 escalation.
   - Elite response SKU (PR-S2): 24x7 P1 (15m), P2 (1h), dedicated escalation manager and runbook playbook.

Next steps: if Greenline wants the pilot credit, we need a signed MPA and a short pilot addendum. Lena — if procurement sends a PO template we can attach the credit addendum to the initial SOW. Ben, can you confirm whether the pilot credit changes any billing recognition constraints?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-premium-pack-quote-v3.pdf
From: Lena Ortiz <procurement@greenline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on premium response SKU and pilot credits

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clarity. A few procurement items before we loop legal: 

- PO: Please populate the attached PO template and return with the signed MPA.
- Credit accounting: we prefer credits to be applied to retainer fees first (so our initial consumption of burst overage is billed directly). Is that doable?
- W-9 and Certs: we need a current W-9 and SOC 2 attestation. SOC 2 is fine to link to your compliance portal if you prefer.

If you can return the PO + metadata and the invoice example by EOD Thursday we can kick legal review immediately.

Regards,
Lena Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager
Greenline Systems

Attachment: greenline-po-template.docx (referenced)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 12:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on premium response SKU and pilot credits

Lena —

We can reverse the credit application order for Greenline: credits will be applied to retainer fees first per your ask. Two notes:

- That adjustment will reduce the pilot credit exposure on Redwood's revenue recognition side; our finance team requires the signed MAP specifying credit order and the 3-month pilot dates.
- W-9 and SOC 2: attaching pointers. SOC 2 link: https://compliance.redwood.ai/soc2/2027-summary, W-9 attached.

I've attached an updated MAP workbook (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) that includes the credit application language and a sample mock invoice showing the pilot credit applied to the retainer line and then to usage if any remains.

Ben Carter
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, redwood-w9.pdf
